question: What is the token threshold at which the catch-all session escalation triggers?
gold: ESCALATION_DEFAULTS enumerates exactly five stop-and-ask triggers, all default true: ambiguous_intent, irreversible_action, low_confidence_high_impact, repeated_failure, scope_expansion (tunable per-workspace via POST /config {escalation}). Separately, CATCHALL_ESCALATE_TOKENS=1e6: a catch-all session node burning 1M tokens with ZERO graph-visible output raises a 'review' escalation.
title: Five escalation triggers ship default-ON; catch-all burns at 1e6 tokens

question: What is the minimum number of consecutive sub-epsilon or no-win rounds required to trigger a converge/stuck state in the optimize loop?
gold: OPTIMIZE_DEFAULTS spreads optimize.DEFAULTS = { epsilon: 0.01, diminishing_rounds: 3 }: epsilon is the per-cycle improvement below which a round counts as diminishing; K=3 consecutive sub-epsilon/no-win rounds trigger converge/stuck. A negative/NaN knob falls back to default (a mis-set knob must not silently disable the control). Budget reuses the loop's tokenBudget — no separate knob.
title: Optimize-loop convergence defaults: epsilon=0.01, diminishing_rounds=3

question: What is the minimum overlap score required to flag a candidate as a likely re-plan duplicate, and what two conditions must the matched task satisfy for the warning to trigger?
gold: SUGGEST_DUP_THRESHOLD=0.6: a candidate scoring >=0.6 label/summary overlap is flagged a likely re-plan duplicate, but ONLY when the matched task is in an OPEN status and kind !== 'note'. Notes and terminal tasks never trigger the dup warning.
title: suggest_links dup threshold 0.6 fires only on OPEN non-note tasks

question: What cosine similarity threshold gates both `autowireNoteProvider` and `autowireNewTaskWholeGraph` in the semantic autowire path?
gold: SEMANTIC_AUTOWIRE_THRESHOLD=0.55 gates both autowireNoteProvider and autowireNewTaskWholeGraph. It scores matches semantically over the WHOLE graph (a deliberate move away from lexical fusion, which regressed). This is the note/task auto-edge creation path — distinct from the RAG recall path.
title: Semantic autowire gated at cosine 0.55 (whole-graph, lexical-fusion dropped)

question: What is the specific cosine similarity value that RAG_RECALL_THRESHOLD uses to gate noteRagCandidates, and why is it set lower than the 0.55 autowire bar?
gold: RAG_RECALL_THRESHOLD=0.40 gates noteRagCandidates: it returns up to `top` candidates with cosine>=0.40 for the AGENT to adjudicate. The value is intentionally lower than the 0.55 autowire/precision bar — recall is the goal here because a human/agent filters the results, so false positives are cheap.
title: RAG recall threshold 0.40 is a RECALL bar, deliberately below the old 0.55 precision bar

question: What is the idle timeout duration after which the embed sidecar exits to free approximately 150MB RSS when no `/embed` requests are received?
gold: lib/embed-server.js is a detached MiniLM sidecar (Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2, 384 dims) that OUTLIVES daemon restarts. It exits on HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT=2min with no /ping (daemon died without clean shutdown) OR IDLE_MS=30min with no /embed (frees ~150MB RSS). On daemon restart embed.js reconnects to the running sidecar — no model re-load.
title: Embed sidecar self-terminates: 2min no-heartbeat, 30min idle; MiniLM-L6-v2/384d

question: What is the default number of days after which terminal tasks and superseded notes are excluded from the default /state payload, and what config endpoint overrides it?
gold: DEFAULT_ARCHIVE_DAYS=14 (override via POST /config {archive_after_days}): terminal tasks (done/canceled) and superseded notes older than the window are excluded from the default /state payload. But anything frontierKeep retains is never archived (a done dep that's still an important context provider stays). Archived nodes stay on disk and remain queryable via /search + suggest_links.
title: Archive window 14 days; frontier-retained nodes are NEVER archived

question: What is the cosine range of the last (open-ended) band in the judge-journal's DEFAULT_BANDS configuration?
gold: DEFAULT_BANDS = [0.25-0.30],[0.30-0.35],[0.35-0.40],[0.40-0.45],[0.45-0.50],[0.50,Infinity] — half-open [lo,hi) buckets for keepRateByBand, last band open-ended. The journal records each edge's creation cosine specifically so a future threshold re-tune is possible; previously prunes deleted the edge with no trace.
title: Judge-journal default cosine bands; last band is open-ended 0.50+

question: What specific routes in mcp-core replay a recorded response on a duplicate op_id to prevent write duplication?
gold: mcp-core's makeCall retries connection-level failures, and a retry can DUPLICATE a write that landed (ECONNRESET after delivery, before response). Routes that mint state per call (/overlay/note, /overlay/knowledge, /overlay/status) replay a recorded response on a duplicate op_id. Only SUCCESS responses are cached (errors are deterministic to re-derive); /overlay/edge needs no cache because addEdge already dedupes on (from,to,fromWorkspace). Persisted LRU survives restart.
title: op_id idempotent-replay protects non-idempotent POSTs from retry duplication

question: What leniency bonus is applied to live nodes in the frontierKeep BFS, and what is the resulting threshold formula for those nodes?
gold: frontierKeep BFS keeps a node at hop depth D if its edge weight >= D*0.30. Blocking edges use weight 1.0; context edges use stored weight defaulting to 0.5. Live nodes (not_ready/ready/in_progress) get a 0.2 leniency bonus: max(0, D*0.30-0.2). Natural caps: blocking reaches 3 hops for done/note, 4 hops for live; a 0.5 context edge survives only 1 hop (done) / 2 hops (live).
title: Frontier keep formula: threshold=depth*0.30, blocking=1.0, context=0.5, live +0.2 leniency

question: What value of `opts.origin` is used to isolate the threshold-gated population in `keepRateByBand`, and what `origin` type made up the entire sub-0.40 KEEP band in live data?
gold: keepRateByBand takes opts.origin to isolate the threshold-gated population. Live data showed the sub-0.40 KEEP band was ENTIRELY hand-asserted note->task edges (origin:'asserted'), never the lexical autowire path the threshold actually gates — folding them together corrupts the tuning curve. Rows missing `origin` (pre-stamping journals) match nothing when a filter is given.
title: Sub-0.40 KEEP band is all hand-asserted edges, not the autowire path the threshold gates

question: What are the three shadow fields added in judge-journal schema v2, and what is the valid range for the confidence field?
gold: Schema v2 added shadow_verdict (keep|prune), shadow_conf (0.0-1.0), and model_version (e.g. 'sonnet-4-6') — the learned model's verdict recorded in SHADOW mode before it ever enforces. Absent on legacy rows (treat missing as null) and ignored by all existing bucket/rate functions, so reads stay backward-compatible.
title: Judge-journal v2 shadow fields (added 2026-06-15) feed learned-gate before enforcement

question: What are the five hard-override categories in `lib/ask-gate.js` that always escalate to the user regardless of preference confidence?
gold: lib/ask-gate.js hardOverride() short-circuits BEFORE recall scoring: irreversible, outward, highImpact, scopeExpansion, repeatedFailure decisions always ask the user even on a perfect preference match. Triggered by opts flags OR conservative keyword regexes (delete/drop/purge, publish/deploy/release/email, payment/charge/refund, scope creep, repeated failure). A confident learned preference can never license one of these.
title: ask-gate ships 5 hard-override categories that ALWAYS escalate regardless of confidence

question: What is the `cosThreshold` value used as the top-1 cosine floor in `lib/ask-gate.js`?
gold: DEFAULTS in lib/ask-gate.js: cosThreshold 0.50 (top-1 cosine floor), gapThreshold 0.25 (external-gap token recurrence), marginThreshold 0.08 (alt sharp-standalone-hit path), localityThreshold 2 (>=2 of 4 project-locality cats), requireEmpirical true (a bare topical note never predicts). These gate whether request_guidance silently predicts instead of escalating.
title: ask-gate predict-vs-ask thresholds are concrete shipped defaults

question: What are the exact numeric limits (lines and characters) that `hooks/orch-gate-trivial.sh` enforces before a main/dispatcher session must claim a task to proceed with an edit?
gold: hooks/orch-gate-trivial.sh sets TRIVIAL_MAX_LINES=20 and TRIVIAL_MAX_CHARS=800; a main/dispatcher session that hasn't claimed a task may only write patches within BOTH limits (and counter is per-session, reset in classify.sh). Larger edits hard-block and require claiming a task. Sourced by both orch-gate.sh and orch-gate-bash.sh.
title: Unclaimed dispatcher edits are allowed only under a 20-line / 800-char trivial budget

question: What git merge strategy does `.gitattributes` assign to `.graph/**`, and what class of conflicts does it prevent when merging attempt-branch worktrees?
gold: .gitattributes assigns `.graph/** merge=ours` (overriding the older per-file `merge=union` — last matching line wins) because attempt-branch worktrees would otherwise cause delete/modify + checkpoint.json conflicts; the daemon is source of truth so the current branch's .graph wins wholesale, never content-merged. Merge drivers aren't portable, so each clone must run once: `git config merge.ours.driver true`.
title: .graph/** uses merge=ours and needs a one-time per-clone git config

question: What environment variable must be set when running tests via scripts/run-tests.js to prevent them from touching the live daemon?
gold: Sandboxed-daemon convention: any test needing a daemon spawns a private one on a private port with a tmp-dir CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA (pattern in test/app-restart.test.js); tests must not read/mutate real graph state. scripts/run-tests.js runs every test/*.test.js as a child with ZONOID_SKIP_LIVE=1. CI uses `npm ci --omit=optional` to skip the large @xenova/transformers optional dep.
title: Tests must spawn a private sandboxed daemon — never the live :8787

question: What cosine similarity band does the write-time signature guard cover that the recall cluster threshold alone would miss?
gold: lib/judge.js dupClusters() recalls near-duplicate notes at DUP_RECALL_THRESHOLD=0.80; a separate write-time signature guard catches the 0.70–0.80 band that never forms a natural 0.80 cluster. The two mechanisms are intentionally independent so close-but-sub-0.80 pairs don't slip through.
title: Note dedup uses a 0.80 recall cluster threshold plus a 0.70–0.80 write-time signature guard

question: What condition must a `start_task` claim satisfy for the overlay claim path to treat it as a legitimate hook-less worker registration?
gold: The SubagentStart hook does NOT fire for run_in_background Agent-tool spawns (they use .output paths, not .jsonl), so such workers never carry agent_tool_spawn:true. The overlay claim path treats a start_task claim that bears an agent_id AND is backed by a registered worktree as a legitimate hook-less worker and registers it on claim — a claim with no worktree is still refused. Thus the branch_task→start_task order IS the registration.
title: Background (run_in_background) workers self-register via start_task, not the SubagentStart hook

question: What two prefix options can be used to signal that a KB note takes priority over the spec or existing code, and where must each appear?
gold: Project KB convention: when a note contradicts the spec or existing code, the title must start with `OVERRIDE:` or the summary with `SPEC IS INCOMPLETE:`. This prefix signals to consuming agents that the note takes priority and they must NOT dismiss the discrepancy as a note error.
evidence: CLAUDE.md (KB note authoring); note:note-mqfatdr2s67 in graph uses OVERRIDE:
title: Notes overriding spec/code MUST prefix title `OVERRIDE:` or summary `SPEC IS INCOMPLETE:`

question: What specific formatting issue with the embedding tokenizer causes notes using fused tokens like "taskTranscript" to fail to surface for relevant queries?
gold: Titles must use isolated vocabulary matching how agents query ("task transcript" not "taskTranscript", "time window overlap" not "time-window-overlap"). The embedding tokenizer relies on word boundaries; fused tokens produce poor retrieval recall so the note may never surface for the queries it was written to answer.
title: Note titles must use space-separated tokens, not camelCase/hyphenated compounds

question: What specific argument must agents pass to `record_decision` to ensure the DAG provenance edge is created at note-creation time?
gold: Agents creating notes via record_decision must pass wires_to=[current_task_key] so the DAG provenance edge is created at note-creation time. Cosine autowire is best-effort and misses structurally important edges, so structural provenance must be explicit.
title: Note creators MUST pass wires_to=[current_task_key] — do not rely on cosine autowire

question: What file stores the CLA signatures, and on which branch is it kept?
gold: Apache-2.0 licensed but every contributor must sign CLA.md before their first contribution is accepted; .github/workflows/cla.yml runs CLA Assistant (signatures recorded to signatures/version1/cla.json on branch cla-signatures). The CLA grants the maintainer a perpetual right to relicense/sublicense contributions under different (incl. commercial/proprietary) terms so the project can offer dual-licensed editions.
title: Contributions require a CLA enforced by a real GitHub Action, enabling dual-licensing

question: What file demonstrates the sandboxed-daemon pattern that tests should follow when spawning a private daemon on a random port with a tmp-dir CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA?
gold: Sandboxed-daemon convention: any test needing a daemon spawns a private one on a random port with a tmp-dir CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA (pattern in test/app-restart.test.js) and must never read or mutate real graph state. Forgetting this corrupts the operator's live :8787 graph.
title: Tests use a private daemon + tmp-dir CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA, never the live :8787 graph

question: What does the cold-arm-must-fail guard gate in the held-out benchmark pipeline?
gold: bench/heldout/ is the only benchmark this repo claims on: the agent solves from a prose spec with NO test/rubric in the worktree, the frozen artifact is graded by an external held-out suite it never saw, and a cold-arm-must-fail guard gates any win claim. The only arm difference is graph access during solve.
title: The shipped benchmark is held-out grading: prose spec in, external suite the agent never sees grades it

question: What are the three specific conditions that must ALL hold simultaneously for retrieved memory to let an agent solve cases it otherwise cannot?
gold: The standing proven claim: retrieved memory lets an agent solve cases it otherwise cannot ONLY when all three hold - (1) empirical (found by running, not derivable from spec), (2) external to the artifact (nothing in-worktree reveals it), (3) project-local (absent from the model's pretraining prior). Violate any one and memory is a null or a tax.
title: Memory is load-bearing iff the knowledge is empirical, external-to-artifact, AND project-local

question: What were the exact warm scores on the two held-out edge case evaluations, and by what multiples did the warm agent write more artifact than the cold agent?
gold: On held-out edge cases the agent never saw, cold scored 0/10 and 0/8 with zero variance; warm scored 8.8/10 and 8/8. Warm wrote 3.8x and 1.7x MORE artifact (citing the seeded note), so the win is retrieve-and-apply (added capability), not shortcutting. These are the actual project-local measured numbers.
title: Causal win measured at n=2: cold 0/10 and 0/8, warm 8.8/10 and 8/8, warm wrote MORE code

question: What fraction of the 52 completed note-dependent tasks are winnable, and which specific slice of tasks does that fraction apply to?
gold: Of 52 completed note-dependent tasks, ~23% (12/52) are winnable - the project-local-measured-facts slice, NOT the general-infra slice (pretraining covers that: 0/4 traps survived in Phase 1). Carries an explicit self-similar-corpus caveat: the corpus is the orchestrator benchmarking itself, so the category transfers but not the 23% point estimate.
title: Winnable-regime frequency on this corpus is ~23% (12/52), resting on project-local facts

question: What was the cost multiplier observed when injecting a forced full payload of approximately 25k characters compared to the ON/OFF baseline?
gold: Forced full payload (~25k chars) cost 1.63x ON/OFF; lean payload (~1-3k chars) cost 1.03x. The whole cost difference is cache_read on the injected payload - output tokens (real work) never moved. Lean injection is cost-neutral. Measure work with output_tokens; headline on cost-weighted gross (cache_read bills ~0.1x).
title: Injection cost = payload size only; the entire ON/OFF gap is cache_read, work never moved

question: What was the relative performance of the combined DAG+RAG arm compared to other arms in terms of hardness tax?
gold: Eight consecutive nulls on self-solvable tasks; forced/precise context only added deliberation (monotone in amount injected, up to ~2x hardness tax - the combined DAG+RAG arm was the WORST). v7 proved semantic retrieval demonstrably worked and changed nothing - recall quality was never the limiter, so don't blame/tune retrieval to chase wins.
title: Forced context imposes up to ~2x over-deliberation tax; the blocker was never recall

question: What specific method did the cold agent use to solve all 3 wincase-c test cases despite a strategy-silent prose spec?
gold: wincase-c's rigging guard did NOT hold - cold solved 3/3 by reading the committed acceptance test, whose generator exposes expected behavior, no matter how strategy-silent the prose spec is. A fully-specified committed test (or dependency source, see silent-cap) for a pure function leaves no empirical gap. This is structural, not a spec-writing flaw - production is naturally held-out, the bench had to be re-engineered to look like it.
title: The oracle leak: an in-worktree test/dependency IS the answer key, so the agent reverse-engineers it

question: What specific flaw in bench v1-v7 caused baselines to overstate self-solvability, and at which version was this flaw detected?
gold: The first seven ON-vs-OFF benchmark versions shipped their acceptance tests inside the agent's worktree, so every cold baseline overstated self-solvability (caught by the rigging guard on the eighth). v1-v7 are gitignored, excluded from the release, and carry no claims. Only bench/heldout/ ships.
title: Bench v1-v7 are contaminated and excluded from the release - make NO claims on them

question: What specific problem occurs when the same hook events are wired in both `.claude/settings.json` and `.cursor/hooks.json`?
gold: When merging adapters/cursor/settings.sample.json into .claude/settings.json, do not additionally wire the same events in .cursor/hooks.json - both fire and the gate/mint hooks run twice. The CLI even emits a warning for the native-.cursor/hooks.json path.
title: Cursor: do NOT also wire the same hook events in .cursor/hooks.json - double execution

question: What specific MCP-side condition does the daemon check when refusing a `start_task` or `merge` claim in harnesses where session hooks have degraded?
gold: The edit-gate is defense-in-depth: session hooks are the front line, but in harnesses/modes where hooks degrade (Cursor CLI -p, cloud, Codex), the daemon's MCP-side refusal on start_task/merge (rejects a claim with no registered worktree) remains the enforcement backstop. Don't assume removing hooks removes the gate.
title: When session hooks don't fire, MCP-side daemon refusal on start_task/merge is the backstop

question: What command must each developer run once in their clone to activate the custom merge driver that prevents `.graph/**` conflicts?
gold: The daemon is the source of truth for graph state, so .gitattributes assigns '.graph/** merge=ours' - on any merge the current branch's .graph wins wholesale, never content-merged (avoids delete/modify + checkpoint.json conflicts from attempt-branch worktrees). Merge drivers aren't portable, so each fresh clone needs the one-time 'git config merge.ours.driver true' or merges break.
title: .graph/** is merge=ours; every clone must run 'git config merge.ours.driver true' once

question: What specific attribution mechanism caused ON's cache_read tokens to be incorrectly bucketed as 'plumbing', making it appear to use 65% less work?
gold: Early reporting used net tokens and saw ON look like 0.35x ('65% less work') - but attributionMcpServer tagging is sticky across post-call messages, bucketing most of ON's cache_read into 'plumbing'. Pure artifact, retracted. Use output_tokens (or fresh input+output) as the work measure, not net.
title: The net = gross - plumbing token metric was a retracted artifact of sticky MCP attribution

question: What are the three driver-death failure modes that cost real runs when waiting on bench driver processes?
gold: Three driver-death failure modes cost real runs: macOS has no 'timeout' coreutil (scripts assuming it die silently), detached/background drivers get orphaned and killed, and watching for output files gives FS read-cache false positives. The only reliable wait is foreground 'kill -0' polling on the child PID.
title: Bench driver waits must be foreground 'kill -0' polling on the child PID

question: What were the exact scores of the warm/ON arm on the two held-out edge case evaluations, and by what factors did it write more code than the cold/OFF arm?
gold: On held-out edge cases the agent never saw, the cold/OFF arm scored 0/10 and 0/8 with ZERO variance; the warm/ON arm scored 8.8/10 and 8/8 and wrote 3.8x and 1.7x MORE code citing the seeded note — so the effect is retrieve-and-apply (added capability), not shortcutting. This is the load-bearing result the whole memory-RAG program rests on.
title: The two causal memory wins: cold 0/10 & 0/8, warm 8.8/10 & 8/8 (blind-graded)

question: What are the three specific counterexample categories that each break one of the load-bearing conditions for memory?
gold: All three conditions are necessary. Counterexamples that each break one: v4 (general verdict didn't help — not empirical), wincase-c/silent-cap (in-worktree test or dependency source IS the oracle — not external), Phase 1 (mkcert issuer-trust, don't-clobber-native-files, GC retention, stale-claim hygiene — general knowledge already in the model's prior, so cold passed every edge, proxy precision 0/4).
title: Memory is load-bearing iff knowledge is empirical AND external-to-artifact AND project-local

question: What three trap classes did the 'cold must fail before warm runs' guard catch as false wins?
gold: Every held-out experiment requires the cold arm to genuinely fail before a warm win can be claimed. This guard caught wincase-c, silent-cap, and all four Phase 1 traps as false wins (cold solved them by reading the committed oracle). Eight nulls plus guard discipline is WHY the two real wins are believable — the failure modes are the trust mechanism, not embarrassments to bury.
title: Rigging guard 'cold must fail before warm runs' is the honesty mechanism — it killed 3 trap classes

question: What specific flaw caused bench versions v1 through v8 to systematically overstate self-solvability?
gold: An in-worktree acceptance test or dependency source IS the oracle — the agent reverse-engineers the strategy from asserted behavior no matter how strategy-silent the prose spec is. So all of v1–v8 systematically OVERSTATED self-solvability (cold arms graded themselves against a visible answer). Fix: the held-out protocol (scripts/bench-heldout.js) gives prose spec only and grades with an external suite the agent never sees. Production is naturally held-out.
title: The oracle leak: every bench v1–v8 shipped its own answer key into the worktree

question: What was the token-equivalent cost avoided by the context-need gate abstaining on the 11 negative-labeled tasks?
gold: The context-need gate (default ABSTAIN) refuses injection on all 11 negative-labeled tasks with zero regret, avoiding ~690,510 token-equivalents of the over-deliberation tax the always-inject arms paid (forced full-payload injection cost 1.63x and up to a ~2x hardness tax monotone in amount injected).
title: Context gate abstains on all 11 negatives at regret 0, avoiding ~690,510 tok-eq of inject tax

question: What is the minimum cosine similarity score (`cosThreshold`) a top result must reach before context injection is triggered, and why was it lowered from the previous default?
gold: lib/context-gate.js DEFAULTS: cosThreshold 0.50 (lowered from 0.55 because the first real positive sat at 0.548), gapThreshold 0.25, marginThreshold 0.08 (alt path), requireEmpirical true, localityThreshold 2. INJECT iff top1>=0.50 AND top note empirical AND (gap>=0.25 OR margin>=0.08) AND projectLocality>=2; else ABSTAIN. These are provisional, calibrated on n=1 positive.
title: Context-gate shipped DEFAULTS: cos 0.50, gap 0.25, margin 0.08, empirical=true, locality 2

question: What is the external-gap score threshold value used to discriminate load-bearing notes from topical noise when MiniLM cosine scores fall within the 0.50–0.55 band?
gold: MiniLM pulls topically-adjacent orchestrator notes into a tight 0.50–0.55 cosine band where neither cosine nor margin can separate a load-bearing note from topical noise. The discriminating signal is external-gap: the fraction of the note's own content tokens that recur in the task text — 0.34 for the on-task scar vs <=0.17 for every plain topical negative.
title: external-gap (not cosine/margin) is the gate's discriminator — MiniLM packs notes into a 0.50–0.55 band

question: What are the four regex categories that contribute to the projectLocality score, and what is the minimum count required to pass the gate?
gold: Phase 1's third boundary (project-locality) is operationalized as a 0–4 count over measured (percentages/ratios), errval (NaN/error codes/quoted data with digits), ident (camelCase/snake_case/file paths/function calls), and observed-on-real-data language. Winners score 3–4; pretraining-prior false-injects score 0–1; only ~14% of the live KB scores >=2. The locality regex structurally can't see migration-schema facts phrased without identifiers/observational language (legacy-id false-negative).
title: projectLocality scores 4 regex categories (measured/errval/ident/observed); gate requires >=2

question: Where does the system track cumulative savings versus judge infrastructure spend, and what ensures judge tokens never appear in per-task ON_cost?
gold: The judge drain runs in a SEPARATE harness session, so its tokens never appear in ON_cost. The system ledger (bench/economy/ledger.json) tracks cumulative savings vs judge infrastructure spend as a separate line — judge tokens are not amortized per task.
title: Judge cost is infrastructure capex, tracked separately — never in per-task ON_cost

question: What is the correct accounting unit for evaluating judge-edge value, given that per-edge amortization is impossible?
gold: A note that improves Task A's summary also benefits every downstream task inheriting A as context, so judge-edge value cannot be amortized per edge. The correct accounting unit is the system ledger's total-savings-vs-total-spend, not any per-task or per-edge ratio.
title: Judge edge value fans out transitively through the DAG, so per-edge amortization is impossible

question: What are the two conditions that must both be true for a trial to be labeled `needs_context` under the Phase 1 held-out ground truth definition?
gold: Phase 1 / held-out ground truth defines needs_context as the strong criterion: cold arm never solved across all trials AND warm arm solved. Derived from bench/heldout/p1/results.jsonl. This is the stricter of the two label schemes used in this repo.
title: needs_context label = cold(OFF) NEVER solved AND warm(ON) solved (held-out derivation)

question: What specific criterion does Phase 1 held-out use to label a case as `needs_context`, as opposed to the cost-weighted metric used in v1–v7 benchmark headlines?
gold: The v1–v7 benchmark headline labels needs_context by a cost-weighted metric (ON underperforms OFF), while Phase 1 held-out uses the stronger 'cold arm never solved' criterion. They reach consistent gate verdicts but are NOT the same definition — don't conflate the two when reading numbers across reports.
title: GOTCHA: two different needs_context label derivations across the benchmark reports

question: What is the specific reason that graph-dependent and wincase-c are excluded from scoped regret despite the gate firing on them?
gold: graph-dependent and wincase-c retrieve the SAME note as the positive and are textually NEARER to it, so the recalibrated gate fires on them (2/2). They are NOT counted in scoped regret only because the note post-dates them (it could not have been retrieved at their run time). This proves a structural limit: a note<->task gate cannot detect held-out-ness — that property is environmental, external to the gate's inputs.
title: Same-micro-domain controls fire the gate but are excluded from regret on temporal grounds

question: What percentage of agent records in the registry lack a session and can only be recovered via time-window-overlap correlation against byWindow?
gold: The task-transcript / resolveOwner held-out win: the spec describes only direct + session resolution, but ~40% of this registry's agent records have no session and are recoverable ONLY by time-window-overlap correlation against byWindow. That fact lives in a pre-seeded note (originally note-mq7kyiir6sx); the OFF arm must derive the strategy from scratch and never references byWindow.
title: resolveOwner win rests on ~40% of registry records lacking a session, recoverable only via byWindow

question: What specific percentage figure represents the self-similar corpus's POI (point of interest) rate that may not transfer to customer projects?
gold: All benchmark numbers come from one operator running the orchestrator instrumenting its OWN memory system — maximally self-similar. What transfers to a customer project is the CATEGORY (every project accumulates its own local empirical facts), not the notes themselves and not necessarily the 23% point estimate.
title: Standing caveat: the corpus is maximally self-similar (orchestrator benchmarking itself)

question: What fraction of the "winnable" tasks fall into the "benchmark-meta" category versus the "transfer-robust general-infra" category according to Phase 0a's split?
gold: Phase 0a found 18/52 'winnable' (external-gap + empirical + load-bearing), splitting them 12 'benchmark-meta' (project-local measured verdicts) vs 6 'transfer-robust general-infra'. Phase 1 INVERTED Phase 0a's bet: the general-infra slice is exactly what pretraining covers (0/4 traps survived), while the project-local-meta slice is where both real wins live. Honest frequency = ~23% (12/52), not the general-infra slice Phase 0a guessed at ~10–15%.
title: Winnable regime is ~23% (12/52) of note-dependent tasks — the project-local-measured slice

question: What was the approximate hardness multiplier from the lowest-context arm (H_off) to the highest-context arm (dagrag) in the v4 measurement?
gold: First real semantic RAG (MiniLM) + DAG context, 4 arms x 2 tasks: NO win on all 6 ON cells, and the combined DAG+RAG arm was the worst. Hardness rose monotonically with amount injected (v4: H_off 14,584 -> search 16,274 -> lean 19,969 -> dagrag 29,027, ~2x). Solve rate stayed 100% everywhere — context only added deliberation. v7 also closed the retrieval-quality alibi: semantic retrieval demonstrably worked and changed nothing; the blocker was never recall.
title: v7: the combined DAG+RAG arm was the WORST; hardness grows monotone in context amount

question: What billing rate do prompt-cache reads incur under `claude -p`, and what effect does this have on cost across both arms of the comparison?
gold: The audited ~90% memory-product savings compare against replaying full conversation history every turn — a baseline nobody competent runs. Under claude -p, prompt-cache reads bill at ~0.1x input and climb monotonically within a session, so the harness gives memory-like cost behavior to BOTH arms for free. Against real baselines the savings evaporate; cost difference was purely cache_read on the injected payload, with output tokens (real work) unmoved.
title: Vendor '90% token savings' is strawman-relative; prompt caching already gives both arms memory-like cost

question: What is the minimum cosine similarity score required for the top retrieved note to pass the context-gate injection check in lib/context-gate.js?
gold: lib/context-gate.js INJECTs a retrieved note only if ALL hold: top1 cosine >= 0.50 (cosThreshold) AND the top note classifies as 'empirical' (requireEmpirical) AND (margin >= 0.08 OR externalGap >= 0.25) AND projectLocality >= 2 of 4 (localityThreshold). Anything else ABSTAINS. Conservative by construction so every miss is a false-negative (missed win), never a wasted inject.
title: Context-gate inject rule: ABSTAIN by default; the exact 5-threshold gate

question: What is the approximate external-gap value of the true positive that distinguishes it from topical near-ties in the 0.50–0.55 MiniLM cluster?
gold: The first real positive sat at top1=0.548 inside a tight 0.50-0.55 MiniLM topical cluster where neither a raw cosine cut nor a margin cut can separate the true scar from topical near-ties. The external-gap (fraction of the note's content tokens that recur in the task text) does: positive ~0.34 vs every topical negative <=0.17. Thresholds are provisional, calibrated on n=1, and fragile to note supersession (a replacement note can drift below the floor).
title: cosThreshold was lowered 0.55->0.50; external-gap, not cosine/margin, discriminates

question: What text markers qualify a note as "principle" type yet disqualify it from inject?
gold: classifyNoteType derives empirical|principle|neutral purely from text markers (overlay addNoteNode stores no type). An empirical signature wins even if principle words also appear, but pure-principle phrasing ('always/never/best practice/prefer/generally') is DISQUALIFIED from inject because the base model already knows principles. Consequence: phrasing a genuine scar as a principle silently makes it non-injectable.
title: Note TYPE is inferred from text by regex — notes carry no explicit type field

question: What are the four categories a note must hit at least two of to pass the projectLocality guard?
gold: A note must hit >=2 of {measured (%/ N/M ratio), errval (NaN/ERR_/quoted digit/exit code), ident (camelCase/snake_case/path/call), observed ('empirically/discovered/observed/measured')} or the gate ABSTAINS 'non-local' even when the fact IS project-local. A migration-schema note written as plain prose scored locality=1 and was rejected; adding a function name like parseTaskId() or 'discovered empirically' pushes it to 2 and clears the guard.
title: projectLocality guard needs >=2 of 4 categories — phrasing alone can sink a real note

question: What file path patterns are in the fixed allow-list that permits writes without a claim in the orch-gate?
gold: The pre-tool claim gate (hooks/orch-gate.js) allows writes without a claim only for a fixed list: .claude/projects/**/memory/, .claude settings/keybindings/launch.json, .mcp.json, CLAUDE.md, .claude/orchestrator/tasks/, .claude/tasks/, /scratch/, *.log and /logs/. It deliberately does NOT exempt /tmp (//private/tmp) or .claude/orchestrator/ source. It also FAILS OPEN: no session_id, daemon unreachable, or orch-off all -> allow.
title: orch-gate FAILS OPEN and exempts a fixed allow-list; /tmp and orch source are NOT exempt

question: What is the cosThreshold value shared by both lib/context-gate.js and lib/ask-gate.js?
gold: lib/context-gate.js (inject-vs-abstain) and lib/ask-gate.js (predict-vs-ask) share the SAME four-guard shape and calibrated DEFAULTS: cosThreshold 0.50, gapThreshold 0.25 (external-gap), marginThreshold 0.08, localityThreshold 2 (of 4 project-locality categories), requireEmpirical true. Both default to the safe action (abstain / ask) and only fire on a high-confidence, specific, project-local, empirical note match. Change one set of thresholds and you almost certainly want to change the other.
title: context-gate and ask-gate are twin abstain/ask-by-default gates with identical shipped thresholds

question: What is the cosine floor value that the discriminator was lowered to, and why does neither raw cosine nor top1-top2 margin cut work as a separator for MiniLM's topically-adjacent orchestrator notes?
gold: MiniLM pulls a tight cluster of topically-adjacent orchestrator notes into a 0.50-0.55 cosine band, so neither a raw cosine cut nor a top1-top2 margin cut separates a true positive from useless-but-topical matches. The discriminating signal is external-gap (fraction of the note's content tokens recurring in the task text): the one real positive measured externalGap 0.34 vs every topical negative <=0.17. The cosine floor was dropped from 0.55 to 0.50 because the only positive label (resolveOwner / note-mq7kyiir6sx) sat at top1=0.548, margin=0.017 and the old gate abstained and MISSED the win. Thresholds are calibrated on n=1 positive — provisional.
title: external-gap, not cosine/margin, is the load-bearing discriminator; cosine floor was lowered 0.55->0.50

question: What specific characteristic must a note have to pass the `requireEmpirical` and `projectLocality` guards, rather than being rejected as a general principle?
gold: requireEmpirical and the projectLocality guard mean a note must be concrete project-local scar-tissue (a gotcha, a decision-with-reason, a root cause) to be injected or to predict a user preference. General PRINCIPLES ('always prefer X', 'best practice') deliberately do NOT qualify — the base model already knows them, so injecting them is pure overhead. A vague topical note will never clear the gate, which is why KB authoring guidance insists notes be written empirically and project-locally.
title: Only EMPIRICAL project-local notes can fire the gates; general principles/best-practices are rejected by design

question: What condition must be met for `lib/ask-promote.js` to flip the live decider from the heuristic to the learned classifier?
gold: The hand-tuned heuristic is the live decider by default. A separately-trained logistic classifier (scripts/ask-clf-*) runs ALONGSIDE in shadow, writing shadow_decision/shadow_conf to .graph/ask-journal.jsonl as training signal WITHOUT deciding. lib/ask-promote.js runs a comparator each cycle and only flips .graph/ask-clf/mode.json from 'heuristic' to 'learned' (one-way, shadow->enforce) once the model beats the heuristic by a margin over a stable window. A missing model/mode file degrades to pure heuristic, so the gate stays usable offline. Same pattern mirrors edge-clf/mode.json.
title: Learned ask/edge classifiers run in SHADOW; live source flips heuristic->learned only via a one-way promotion

question: What specific costs did the benchmark identify as the reason orchestrator-ON arms performed worse than OFF on self-solvable tasks?
gold: The gates default to abstain because the benchmark found that on self-solvable tasks every orchestrator-ON arm did MORE work than OFF — injecting context the model didn't need is not free: it pays consult-overhead C (cache cost to hold the graph) AND nudges the model into extra deliberation. The whole point of the context-need gate is to suppress that tax by injecting only on a confident empirical match. This is why 'predict by default / inject only when confident' is a hard project stance, not mere caution.
title: Abstain-by-default exists to avoid the 'over-deliberation tax' measured in bench/report-v2..v7

question: What specific fields are captured in the frozen snapshot that `buildGraph` stores in `overlay.snapshots` when it first encounters a Claude native task?
gold: When buildGraph first sees a Claude native task it adopts a frozen snapshot ({subject, description, status, blockedBy, owner, metadata, snapshotted_at}) into overlay.snapshots; that snapshot — not the native .json file — is authoritative for structure. When the native file is later removed by the cleanupPeriodDays retention sweep, aggregateWorkspace falls back to the snapshot, so tasks don't vanish from the graph. Editing only the native file won't necessarily win.
title: Overlay snapshot is authoritative for task structure; the native file is a live echo

question: What value does `emitDiff` write to `status_changed` when a task's status override is present in the previous overlay but absent in the new one?
gold: emitDiff writes status_changed -> 'ready' for any task whose status override is ABSENT in the new overlay but present in prev (i.e. the override was deleted, e.g. on releaseClaim). On rehydrate the code explicitly skips node.status === 'ready' so the sentinel is never persisted back as a real status. Treating 'ready' as a stored status value will corrupt the diff logic.
title: status:'ready' is a SENTINEL in overlay sync meaning 'override cleared', not a real status

question: What condition must be true for a note to be re-pullable by the edge-judge, and what value is stamped on `judgedAtEpoch[key]` when a 'no edge' verdict is reached?
gold: overlay.epoch is a monotonic counter bumped on every note/task ADD. A note is re-pullable by the edge-judge only when judgedAtEpoch[key] < epoch; a 'no edge' verdict stamps judgedAtEpoch[key]=epoch so it stays out of the queue until the graph actually changes. judgeCursor persists the judge's queue position across daemon restarts so it never re-walks the whole graph. judgedClusters is the node-dedup analogue keyed by cluster signature.
title: Incremental edge-judge gates on epoch / judgedAtEpoch / judgeCursor — not on cosine alone

question: What is the `delaySeconds` value used for the idle heartbeat `ScheduleWakeup` when no loop is active?
gold: When no loop is active the system tells the agent to call loop_control({action:'start', tokenBudget:5000000, maxIterations:6250, minPoll:30, maxPoll:300, batch:4, maxConcurrency:6}). The idle heartbeat ScheduleWakeup uses delaySeconds=7200 (2h). These exact defaults govern autonomous-loop cost/cadence and can't be guessed off-repo.
title: Shipped default heartbeat loop controls: 5M token budget, 6250 iters, 30-300s poll, batch 4, conc 6; idle wakeup 7200s

question: What is the naming convention for the per-attempt frozen directories in `bench/heldout/frozen`, and where are their corresponding graders stored?
gold: bench/heldout/frozen holds frozen attempt dirs named like api-contract-off-0, claim-task-on-gated-0, bench-metric-on-search-1 — the suffix is the experiment arm (orchestrator off vs on, and the on-mode: gated/search/iterative) plus an index, paired with a per-challenge grader in bench/heldout/graders/<challenge>.grader.js. This is how the self-learn benchmark compares conditions; the naming is the contract.
title: Heldout bench fixtures encode A/B arms in the directory name: <challenge>-<off|on>-<gated|search|iterative>-<N>

question: What namespacing format must be used when referencing a task across sessions, and how does native-tasks.js key the unified workspace task list?
gold: Native Claude Code task IDs are local to a session; any cross-session/workspace reference must be the namespaced key `{session-uuid}/{id}`. native-tasks.js unions all session task files into one workspace list keyed this way (deps are intra-session blockedBy, namespaced to the same session).
title: Cross-session task IDs must be namespaced {session}/{id}

question: What is the specific file path layout that `native-tasks.js` wraps, and why is it intentionally the only file that reads it?
gold: The `~/.claude/tasks/{session}/{id}.json` layout (and the projects-dir encoding) is UNDOCUMENTED / internal to Claude Code. native-tasks.js is deliberately the single adapter for it — if a Claude Code version changes the format, only this file should need updating. Don't read those files anywhere else.
title: native-tasks.js is the SOLE adapter for the undocumented on-disk task layout

question: What specific command must be run to make a locally-trusted CA available so the daemon's /mcp endpoint can be served over HTTPS?
gold: A self-signed cert can't shortcut local HTTPS: TLS checks the issuer against the trust store regardless of locality, so `mkcert -install` (adds a locally-trusted CA) is mandatory to serve the daemon's /mcp over HTTPS. This is the only reason the setup wizard insists on mkcert over a hand-rolled cert.
title: mkcert is required because TLS validates the cert issuer, not localhost

question: What is the only surface that renders inline MCP Apps UI in the desktop app, and why do local stdio MCP servers not qualify?
gold: Shipped defaults: PORT=8787 (dashboard/graph), HTTPS_PORT=8788 (/mcp over locally-trusted HTTPS). The HTTPS custom-connector path is the ONLY surface that renders inline MCP Apps UI in the desktop app — local stdio MCP servers do not render it; otherwise you fall back to the preview panel.
title: Daemon ports: HTTP 8787, HTTPS 8788; inline UI only via custom connector

question: What happens to a Write/Edit/Bash-write operation when the orchestrator daemon is unreachable — is it allowed or blocked?
gold: orch-gate.js denies a Write/Edit/Bash-write ONLY on a definitive 'no claim for this session'; if the daemon is unreachable, or the hook itself throws, it allows the edit (fail-open by design — never brick edits). So the gate is a guardrail, not a hard security boundary against a down daemon.
title: The PreToolUse write-gate FAILS OPEN when the daemon is unreachable

question: What specific condition does the gate check to allow a write, and what does it fail to verify about the task's legitimacy?
gold: Once a task has a registered worktree, the gate denies writes outside that worktree path (use the path from branch_task). Honest limit: it checks for a claimed in_progress task + worktree existence, not status truth — a rubber-stamp claim still passes it.
title: Gate enforces writes happen INSIDE the registered worktree, but can't verify task legitimacy

question: What is the maximum number of initiatives the self-learn planner is allowed to output per run?
gold: Hard rules born from a real runaway: the planner NEVER cancels/supersedes/replans an in-flight task (that's the user's call), NEVER duplicates an open task (suggest_links + dedup BEFORE TaskCreate), caps output at 1-3 initiatives, and STOPs rather than fabricate busywork — graph bloat is failure.
title: The self-learn planner is ADDITIVE-ONLY — it caused a runaway once

question: What specific condition causes `decideOptimize` to return `'stuck'` rather than a silent stop reason like `'diminishing'` or `'budget'`?
gold: decideOptimize returns 'stuck' (→ request_guidance) when the last K rounds produced no real win (no winner, or guardrail regression). 'stuck' deliberately outranks the silent stop reasons (diminishing/budget) because a problem failing every round needs human judgement, not a quiet drop. The only human-in-loop path is escalate — NEVER auto-cancel/replan.
title: A stuck optimization ESCALATES to a human, never self-drops or auto-replans

question: What is the decision precedence order used by the optimize loop when determining whether to stop or continue iterating?
gold: DEFAULTS = { epsilon: 0.01, diminishing_rounds: 3 }; mis-set (negative/NaN) knobs fall back to defaults so a bad knob can't silently disable the control. Decision precedence (first match wins): target-converged → stuck → diminishing-converged → budget → iterate.
title: Optimize-loop defaults: epsilon=0.01, diminishing_rounds(K)=3, fixed precedence

question: What environment variable was added to override the `process.cwd()`-based workspace resolution in `mcp-graph.js`?
gold: mcp-graph.js used to post process.cwd() as the daemon workspace on startup, so any process loading the orchestrator MCP (e.g. a headless agent in a git worktree) hijacked the GLOBAL workspace pointer — repointing the live graph and blinding agents to the real workspace's learnings. Now honors ORCH_WORKSPACE when set (else cwd).
title: ORCH_WORKSPACE overrides cwd-as-workspace (dogfood-finding #1)

question: What does PLUMBING capture that causes it to under-count the true overhead, and what should NET be interpreted as as a result?
gold: MCP tool-schema tokens are cached into the system prompt and amortized across the session, NOT attributable per-message. So PLUMBING captures only tool_use/tool_result round-trips and under-counts the always-resident schema overhead. Read NET as an upper bound on work-only cost and PLUMBING as a lower bound on true orchestration overhead.
title: Bench PLUMBING under-counts the always-resident MCP schema tax

question: What is the corroboration guard condition that must be satisfied for a WIN verdict in the v4 benchmark?
gold: The v4 benchmark decomposes each arm into W (real work=diffTokens), H (hardness=output−W), C (consult overhead=ON−OFF cache cost). A WIN needs all four guards: precondition H_off≥2×W_off, fairness both-solve≥0.8, margin METRIC>0 and >pooled stdev, corroboration W_on/W_off≤1.1. Any guard failing → NO-WIN.
title: Bench WIN requires all four guards to PASS; METRIC=(H_off−H_on)×5 − C

question: Where is a cross-workspace ghost edge stored, and how is the foreign node's status resolved?
gold: A dependency on a node in another workspace is a 'ghost edge': it lives in the consumer's overlay (fromWorkspace set means the provider lives elsewhere), and the foreign status is resolved on demand (cached, cycle-guarded) rather than stored. Don't look for it in the provider's graph.
title: Cross-workspace ghost edges store on the CONSUMER, foreign status resolved lazily

question: What status does a code task complete with under the autonomous orch-loop, and what action does the self-learn-judge explicitly NOT perform even after picking a winner?
gold: Under the autonomous orch-loop, every spawned code task works in an isolated orch/attempt/<slug> worktree, commits there, and completes as 'MERGE PENDING' — it never edits the live checkout and never merges to main. The self-learn-judge picks a winner but (in hold-merge mode) does NOT merge; merge is a deliberate human/dispatcher step.
title: Heartbeat-loop code work is hold-merge: completes as MERGE PENDING, never merges to main

question: What does the staleness sweep release, and what cache does it bust when reverting an agent's in_progress claim?
gold: Agent liveness fix #11: /agent/done releases the in_progress task the agent held; a staleness sweep releases abandoned claims (kill/crash/idle/cross-session) before reading native and busts the agg cache so reverted status shows same-build; releaseClaim also reverts native status to keep write-through in sync.
title: /agent/done CASCADES to release the task an agent held (fixes phantom in_progress)

question: What field must `taskTranscript` use to correlate a task's logical assignee with the harness agent record that carries `transcript_path`, given that the two never share a matching key?
gold: A task's recorded assignee is the LOGICAL worker name passed to start_task, but the agent record carrying transcript_path is registered by the SubagentStart hook under an opaque random harness agent_id, so the two never match by key. taskTranscript must correlate by session + claim-window time-overlap (harnessTranscriptForTask) instead of a direct lookup.
title: Task assignee is a logical name; transcript_path lives under a random harness agent_id

question: What condition causes `harnessTranscriptForTask` to return null rather than widening the window?
gold: In harnessTranscriptForTask a missing/unparsable lastChanged becomes Date.now() and an agent with no endedAt (still running) is treated as ending now, so the window widens rather than dropping the row; only a NaN firstSeen (winStart) returns null. Overlap >= 0 (intervals merely touching) counts as a match, and the largest overlap wins.
title: Transcript window-correlation widens, not rejects, on missing bounds

question: What specific note content causes a failure to be excluded from the `rejected[]` ledger in `digestRejected`?
gold: digestRejected's rejected[] = verdict losers (source:'verdict', carrying beatenBy=winner) plus GENUINE dead-end failures (source:'failure'). Failures whose note says superseded/duplicate/consolidated are deliberately excluded because they are replaced work, not dead ends — re-proposing them is fine.
title: rejected[] ledger excludes superseded/duplicate/consolidated failures

question: What condition must be met for the shared-session transcript hop to be allowed by `anySession: taskTokens`?
gold: taskTranscript resolves in order: assignee's own transcript_path -> per-session binding -> harness window-correlation -> the task's shared session transcript. The last (shared-session) hop is gated by anySession: taskTokens allows it ONLY when the session maps to a single task, while /costflow always allows it because splitSessionTokens divides the shared total honestly.
title: Session-transcript token fallback is gated so a shared total isn't painted across many tasks

question: What was the original rate limit for gated searches before it was raised, and why was it increased for bench trials?
gold: checkGatedRateLimit caps gated searches at 20 per rolling 60s window per IP. It was deliberately raised from 3 because all bench trial runs share the 127.0.0.1 bucket and a low limit caused spurious abstains between sequential trials.
title: Gated-search rate limit is 20 calls / 60s per IP (raised from 3 for bench trials)

question: What summary line format must each test file print before exiting, and what exit code does it use when there are failures?
gold: The ~150 files in test/ use no test framework. Each requires the target module directly (e.g. require('../daemon.js')), prints 'PASS <label>'/'FAIL <label>' lines, ends with 'N passed, M failed', and process.exit(fail===0?0:1). New tests must follow this shape rather than reaching for jest/mocha.
evidence: test/rejected-digest.test.js; 151 test/ files match the convention
title: Tests are plain Node with no framework: PASS/FAIL lines, 'N passed, M failed', exit nonzero

question: What percentage of rows in the economy-bench task-transcript grader registry have no transcript_path and no session, requiring attribution solely via byWindow overlap with the task's claim window?
gold: The task-transcript scenario grader (which the agent never sees) builds a registry where ~40% of rows have no transcript_path and no session — attributable ONLY by overlapping the task's claim window against byWindow. The prose spec describes only direct + session lookup, so a spec-faithful impl fails the edge cases; the ON arm's KB note is what seeds the window-overlap fallback. This is the intended OFF-vs-ON delta of the benchmark.
title: economy-bench task-transcript grader injects ~40% correlation-only rows a spec-faithful impl misses
